title: Interval-Calibrated Noisy Quantization: A Parameter-Free Defense Against Quantization-Gap Attacks

contributions.purpose: Defend against quantization-gap attacks without the impractical per-model grid search needed to set noise scale.
contributions.mechanism: Derive the Gaussian noise scale directly from quantization interval half-widths, computing sigma-hat as the median of per-layer half-widths with a single pass over weights and no evaluation data.
contributions.evaluation: The computed sigma-hat falls within 22% of the grid-search optimal sigma*.
contributions.source_quote: A parameter-free defense that derives noise scale from quantization interval statistics, eliminating the need for evaluation-based tuning. Our computed sigma-hat falls within 22% of the grid-search optimal sigma*.

contributions.purpose: Adapt noise magnitude to the differing quantization geometry of individual layers.
contributions.mechanism: Per-layer calibration that sets noise per layer's interval half-width rather than a single global scale.
contributions.evaluation: Improves security by 0.37 percentage points while reducing variance by 56%.
contributions.source_quote: A per-layer calibration approach that adapts noise magnitude to each layer's quantization geometry, improving security by 0.37 percentage points while reducing variance by 56%.

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate that the parameter-free defense preserves both security and utility.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluation on the ELQ attack benchmark (Phi-2 + LLM.int8()) with utility measured across multiple benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 98.77% code security (vs. 33.4% without defense), matching the grid-search baseline (98.17%) within 0.6 percentage points while preserving utility across HumanEval, MBPP, MMLU, and TruthfulQA.
contributions.source_quote: Comprehensive evaluation on the ELQ attack benchmark, demonstrating that our method achieves 98.77% code security (vs. 33.4% without defense), matching the grid-search baseline (98.17%) within 0.6 percentage points while preserving utility across HumanEval, MBPP, MMLU, and TruthfulQA.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Existing defenses (Egashira et al., 2024) inject Gaussian noise before quantization. However, the noise scale sigma must be carefully tuned... Prior work requires per-model grid search over validation sets to find the optimal sigma, which is impractical for deployment... We propose interval-calibrated noisy quantization, a parameter-free defense that derives the noise scale directly from quantization interval geometry.

Li et al. (2024) proposed EFRAP, which learns non-nearest rounding strategies to disrupt backdoor activation, but this approach requires training and is designed for image classification rather than LLMs. Our work addresses the critical gap of determining noise scale without evaluation-based tuning, deriving sigma-hat directly from quantization interval geometry.
